(1) the dimorphic incompatibilities in N. pletata prevent self and intramorphic fertilization and (2) compatible pollen dilution reduces fertility in populations of N. pelata with strongly biased floral morph ratios.

clonal reproduction is common in populations of N. peltata and is associated with a reduction of fertility; clonal propagation does not appear to have led to the breakdown of the heterostylus syndrome in N. p. peltata; the reduction in fertility is not due to changes in floral morphology; and the reduction in fertility appears to be due to pollen limitation, which results from the clonal propagation of a single morph.

The main takeaway from our work is that
clonal growth can constrain the functioning of the distylous syndrome in N. pellata, and that these effects are likely to be common in distylous species.
clonal reproduction can compromise sexual reproduction, but this is unlikely to result in evolutionary changes to the distyly syndrome.

, despite the potential for negative interactions between clonal propagation and sexual reproduction, the dimorphic incompatibilities of distylous N. peltate populations are maintained in the face of clonal interference.
